hadith:
Bathing (Ghusl) - Narrated Maimuna:

I placed water for the bath of the Prophet (ﷺ) and screened him with a garment. He poured water over his hands and washed them. After that he poured water with his right hand over his left and washed his private parts, rubbed his hands with earth and washed them, rinsed his mouth, washed his nose by putting water in it and then blowing it out and then washed his face and forearms. He poured water over his head and body. He then shifted from that place and washed his feet. I gave him a piece of cloth but he did not take it and came out removing the water (from his body) with both his hands.
message: Embrace your faith sincerely, recognizing it as a gift from Allah rather than a favor bestowed upon Him. Reflect on the purity and humility exemplified through the Prophet Muhammad’s ritual bathing, emphasizing cleanliness and devotion. Remember Allah's infinite generosity, inspiring gratitude and compassion towards all creation.
name:
Al Kareem - الْكَرِيمُ - The Most Generous

Originating from Arabic, Al-Kareem is derived from the root word 'k-r-m' which means to be generous or noble. In Islamic theology, this name emphasizes Allah's boundless mercy and His willingness to bestow blessings and sustenance upon His creatures without any expectation in return.
verse:
Al-Hujurat - The Rooms - 49:17

They regard their acceptance of Islam as a favour to you. Tell ˹them, O  Prophet˺, “Do not regard your Islam as a favour to me. Rather, it is Allah Who has done you a favour by guiding you to the faith, if ˹indeed˺ you are faithful.
